blueprint.competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination

deficit_basis.selected_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination

official_outline_path: cardiomyopathy, dilated, including alcoholic, viral, takotsubo

difficulty.basis: Requires integration of an ACS-like presentation, stress context, angiographic exclusion of an obstructive culprit, nonterritorial wall-motion abnormalities, and MRI tissue characterization.

claim_audit.takotsubo_core: PASS — current NCBI review supports transient nonischemic LV dysfunction that mimics ACS, commonly after intense emotional or physical stress.
claim_audit.nonterritorial_wall_motion: PASS — takotsubo wall-motion abnormalities typically extend beyond one epicardial coronary vascular distribution.
claim_audit.no_obstructive_culprit: PASS — absence of obstructive CAD or acute plaque rupture is a central diagnostic feature in the cited framework.
claim_audit.ecg_and_troponin: PASS — ST-segment/T-wave abnormalities and a mild-to-moderate biomarker rise are compatible with the syndrome; the item deliberately uses no numerical cutoff.
claim_audit.mri_pattern: PASS — myocardial edema can occur without a corresponding late-gadolinium-enhancement pattern; the rationale does not assert that LGE is absolutely impossible in takotsubo.
claim_audit.emotional_trigger: PASS — used as a supportive clue, not a mandatory diagnostic requirement.

option_audit.correct: Takotsubo uniquely integrates the stress trigger, ACS mimic, absent obstructive culprit, nonterritorial apical/midventricular dysfunction, basal hyperkinesis, and MRI pattern.
option_audit.anterior_mi: Anterior MI due LAD occlusion is a real ACS mimic, but an LAD-occlusion mechanism does not fit angiography without an obstructive/plaque-rupture culprit and dysfunction extending beyond one coronary territory.
option_audit.myocarditis: Myocarditis can cause chest pain, troponin elevation, ECG changes, and nonischemic dysfunction, but the characteristic stress-associated ballooning pattern plus the stated MRI pattern makes takotsubo the better diagnosis.
option_audit.vasospasm: Vasospasm can produce transient ST elevation with no fixed stenosis, but diagnosis is supported by episodic/nitrate-responsive ischemia or provoked spasm and does not best explain the specified ballooning pattern.
option_audit.pericarditis: Pericarditis is a real ST-elevation mimic but characteristically produces pericarditic pain with diffuse ST/PR changes and pericardial inflammatory findings rather than the stated ventricular ballooning pattern.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: From the vignette alone, the decisive pattern is acute ACS-like symptoms after emotional stress with no obstructive coronary culprit plus apical/midventricular akinesis, basal hyperkinesis, and wall-motion abnormality beyond one vascular territory. Takotsubo is the unique best match.
adversarial_second_pass.minoca_attack: MINOCA is a working syndrome category rather than the specific etiologic diagnosis requested; the vignette supplies a characteristic takotsubo phenotype.
adversarial_second_pass.myocarditis_attack: Myocarditis remains a theoretical mimic, but the convergence of emotional trigger, classic ventricular geometry, absence of obstructive culprit, and lack of a corresponding inflammatory LGE pattern makes it inferior to takotsubo.
adversarial_second_pass.vasospasm_attack: Normal angiography alone could occur after resolved vasospasm, but the specified nonterritorial ballooning with basal hyperkinesis is not explained as well by vasospasm.
adversarial_second_pass.anterior_mi_attack: Anterior ST elevation and troponin elevation initially suggest MI, but the absence of a culprit lesion and non-LAD distribution of systolic dysfunction directly undermine the LAD-occlusion option.
adversarial_second_pass.pericarditis_attack: The stem lacks positional/pleuritic pain, friction rub, diffuse ST elevation, PR depression, effusion, or pericardial inflammation; the ventricular findings point elsewhere.
adversarial_second_pass.cueing_attack: The item does not name 'broken-heart syndrome' or 'apical ballooning syndrome' in the stem. The emotional trigger is one clue among several independent diagnostic findings.
adversarial_second_pass.unsupported_precision_check: No numeric troponin threshold, coronary stenosis percentage, exact recovery time, disease prevalence, age cutoff, or mandatory stress requirement is asserted.
